features.name: Academic qualifications
features.description: Captures the level and strength of the applicant's formal technical education or degree attainment relevant to the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures hands-on experience designing agent-based systems, including architecture, guardrails, supervision, permissions, or supporting control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering problem-solving examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has shipped AI or LLM-backed systems in production and treats reliability, evaluation, or failure modes seriously.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful AI or LLM experience described.
Mentions AI features or interest without production detail.
States they shipped AI or LLM-backed functionality in production.
Shows production maturity by discussing evaluation, reliability, unpredictable inputs, failure modes, or trustworthiness.

features.name: Collaboration and learning posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and willingness to collaborate closely with security specialists or other internal partners.

levels.descriptor: No collaboration signal appears beyond applying for the role.
Cross-functional work is implied, but the posture toward security specialists is not explicit.
The letter explicitly shows enthusiasm for close collaboration with security engineers or learning from specialist teammates.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security work as helping developers through secure defaults, lower friction, empathy for internal users, and workflow-friendly tooling.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor and maintainability mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes correctness, testing, operability, maintenance, reliability, and long-term care as core engineering values.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Evidence and impact specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with specific examples, mechanisms, outcomes, measurements, or visible effects.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on generic assertions with little supporting evidence.
The letter names some tasks or technologies but leaves ownership and outcomes vague.
The letter gives specific owned examples with clear practical effects.
The letter gives especially crisp evidence of impact, such as quantified results or vivid before-and-after operational change.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade Go appears in the applicant's experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures how coherent, distinctive, memorable, and well-structured the letter's overall story and prose flow are beyond mere correctness.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented, hands-on security practice outside routine product engineering, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public codebases through contribution, maintainership, upstream repair, releases, reviews, or serving external users beyond the employer boundary.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the ambition, rigor, and technical substance of self-directed engineering projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned.
Mentions a small or utilitarian personal app or tool with limited technical challenge.
Shows a sustained side project with nontrivial systems, infrastructure, or engineering discipline.
Shows an ambitious distributed, reliability-heavy, or failure-oriented project chosen specifically to tackle hard edge cases.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or systems.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: Captures the breadth and depth of hands-on production ownership the letter conveys through launched, maintained, operated, or otherwise shipped systems.

levels.descriptor: Only one or two launched or maintained services are mentioned, or the scope is vague.
Roughly three or four services are mentioned, showing repeated production ownership.
Five or more services are mentioned, with explicit launch, maintenance, or testing responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the applicant presents, especially in years or overall career duration.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Role-specific security automation fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter understands this exact role as scaling security through automation and maps the applicant's motivations or background to that mission.

levels.descriptor: Interest in the role is generic and could fit many software jobs.
The letter shows some interest in security or backend impact, but the motivation stays broad.
The letter clearly wants to make secure behavior easier by default or reduce repetitive security toil.
The letter offers a nuanced philosophy of security automation as leverage, capacity creation, or quiet resilience.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses through methods like threat modeling, review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the strength of formal third-party security credentials or certifications cited as evidence of security knowledge or skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification or equivalent external validation is mentioned.
The letter cites a baseline knowledge credential, such as Security+.
The letter cites a stronger hands-on credential, such as OSCP.
The letter cites multiple rigorous certifications or another unusually strong form of external security validation.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful view of what security engineering is for and conveys authentic motivation or values around secure systems work.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinctive security philosophy beyond generic enthusiasm.
Shows broad positive sentiment about security or impact, but little deeper framing.
Expresses a clear philosophy about rigor, resilience, secure defaults, or invisible success.
Offers a memorable, specific philosophy that strongly reinforces fit for this kind of security work.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building automation for vulnerability intake, triage, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures surface-level mechanical quality, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures genuinely distinct or idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to any broader recurring construct.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
